roads.name: Rang Sainte-Anne
words: Sweeping and steady: 10 curves in 2.2 miles.
Plenty of tight curves among them.
From 973 to 1,158 ft, with 540 ft of up and down along the way.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every road in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 90 km/h limit its corners still ask for about 0.66 g, so the curves, not the limit, set the pace. Most of it has no posted limit on the map, so this takes Quebec's 90 km/h.

roads.name: Route 277
words: An easygoing road: 8 curves in 4.4 miles, with room to breathe between them.
The curves flow straight into one another.
From 1,129 to 1,513 ft, with 984 ft of up and down along the way.
Homes line much of it: about 48 buildings a mile beside the road.
11 parks, trailheads and other stops along it, so it's likely busier than most, especially on weekends.
